rows.text: Regulation (EU) 2023/1230 governs the placing on the market (REG Art. 3(12); Art. 54 application from 20 January 2027 as corrected by the corrigendum point 10; Art. 51(2) repeal of Directive 2006/42/EC from 20 January 2027 as corrected by point 5). The 10 January 2027 signing date does not matter, since placing is the first making available, and the Art. 52(1) transitional rule only covers products placed before 20 January 2027.

No. On 1 December 2026 Directive 2006/42/EC still governs (Art. 51(2) of the Regulation, corrected, repeals it from 20 January 2027), and its Art. 12(4) allows a non-harmonised Annex IV machine only the EC type-examination (Annex IX) or full quality assurance (Annex X), not unit verification (module G). The Regulation admitting module G applies only from 20 January 2027 (Art. 54).

rows.value: As a manufacturer: under Article 18 of Regulation (EU) 2023/1230 it is considered the manufacturer and subject to the Article 10 manufacturer obligations for the modified machinery (narrowed to the affected item only if the modification affects only a machinery item forming part of an assembly).
rows.text: Under Article 18 (Regulation, applicable from 20 January 2027), a company that carries out a substantial modification is considered a manufacturer and bears the Article 10 manufacturer obligations for that machinery, and must ensure and declare conformity on its sole responsibility. The narrower case (only a part of an assembly affected) is not established by the files for this modification.

Yes. Under Art. 10(7) of the Machinery Regulation (applicable from 20 January 2027, per Art. 54), digital instructions may be provided for professional-only machinery, with paper free of charge on the user's request at purchase (within one month) and online access kept for the expected lifetime and at least 10 years. The univpm guideline's paper requirement comes from the repealed Directive 2006/42/EC.

rows.text: Under Article 15(2) of Regulation (EU) 2023/1230, which applies from 20 January 2027, a distributor must verify before making machinery available on the market that it bears the CE marking, is accompanied by the EU declaration of conformity, is accompanied by the instructions for use and safety information in an understandable language, and that the manufacturer and importer have met their obligations.

Under Article 52(1) of Regulation (EU) 2023/1230, as corrected by the corrigendum (point 6), machines placed on the market in conformity with Directive 2006/42/EC before 20 January 2027 may not be impeded by Member States, so the last day is 19 January 2027.
Under Article 54(c) of Regulation (EU) 2023/1230, as corrected by the corrigendum, Article 6(7) applies from 19 July 2023.
Under Article 53(3) of Regulation (EU) 2023/1230, as corrected, the first specific report was due by 20 July 2026 and repeats every five years, so the second is due by 20 July 2031.

No. Under Article 47(2) of Regulation (EU) 2023/1230, as corrected, the five-year delegation runs from 19 July 2023, so the report is due by 19 October 2027 (nine months before the period ends on 19 July 2028). That deadline has not passed on 14 November 2026.

No. Under Machinery Directive 2006/42/EC Annex II, 1.B (item 6), a partly completed machine must not be put into service until the final machinery has been declared in conformity; the UR10e manual's Declaration of Incorporation (manual p. 227) repeats this for the e-Series robots.

rows.text: Under Directive 2006/42/EC, Article 13(2), the assembly instructions and the declaration of incorporation, once the partly completed machinery is incorporated into the final machinery, form part of the technical file for that final machinery.

rows.text: Under Article 5(1) of Directive 2006/42/EC (in force until 20 January 2027, per Regulation 2023/1230 Art. 51(2)), before machinery is placed on the market and/or put into service the manufacturer or his authorised representative must complete steps (a) to (f); the Article names the manufacturer, not the integrator, so applying these steps to the integrator depends on whether he is the 'manufacturer' under Art. 2(i).

Yes. Under Regulation (EU) 2023/1230, Article 24(3), the CE marking of a vehicle servicing lift (Annex I, Part A, point 3) must be followed by the notified body's identification number, because a 1 March 2027 unit is placed under the Regulation after the Directive's repeal.

The documents do not state a maximum penalty amount applicable in Italy under Regulation (EU) 2023/1230; Article 50 of the Regulation only requires Member States to set penalties that are effective, proportionate and dissuasive.

The files give only the deadline for the first Article 6(10) template implementing act (not later than 20 July 2024, per the Regulation as corrected by the Corrigendum, point 2). They do not record the date on which the Commission actually adopted it.

The files do not name the notified body that carried out the EC type-examination of the MA STAR two-post lift; the manufacturer's EC declaration of conformity (mastar-manual, p. 37) lists directives and standards but no notified body.

The files do not state the date of the EC declaration of conformity for the complete robot cell. The UR manuals (ur10e-manual p. 227) only say the integrator must provide that DOC; the only dated declaration present is the manufacturer's partly-completed-machine DOI dated 20 December 2024.
Article 50(1) of Regulation (EU) 2023/1230 applies from 20 October 2026, under Article 54, third paragraph, point (b), as corrected by Corrigendum point 12.
Under Article 54(a) of Regulation (EU) 2023/1230, as corrected by Corrigendum point 11, Articles 26 to 42 (notification of conformity assessment bodies) apply from 20 January 2024.
Under Article 6(9) of Regulation (EU) 2023/1230, as corrected by the Corrigendum (point 1), Member States must first provide the Article 6(5) data and information by 20 July 2025.
Under Article 53(1) of Regulation (EU) 2023/1230, as corrected by Corrigendum point 8, the Commission must submit its first evaluation and review report by 20 July 2028, and then every four years.
Yes. Under Article 51(2) of the Regulation, as corrected by Corrigendum point 5, Directive 2006/42/EC is repealed with effect from 20 January 2027, so it is still in force on 18 January 2027.
No. Under Article 54 of Regulation (EU) 2023/1230, as corrected by the corrigendum, Article 50(1) (penalties) applies from 20 October 2026, so it does not yet apply on 1 September 2026.

No. Under Article 52(1), second sentence, of Regulation (EU) 2023/1230, as corrected by the corrigendum, Chapter VI applies mutatis mutandis instead of Article 11 of Directive 2006/42/EC only from 19 July 2023, so it did not apply on 15 July 2023.

Yes. Under Article 52(1) of Regulation (EU) 2023/1230, as corrected by the corrigendum to 20 January 2027, a machine placed on the market in conformity with Directive 2006/42/EC on 15 January 2027 is covered, so Member States may not impede its making available on the market on 1 March 2027.

No. Under art. 71 c. 11 of D.Lgs. 81/2008, successive periodic verifications of Annex VII equipment are at the employer's free choice between the ASL and authorised bodies; the 30-day gating in DM 2011 art. 2 c. 8 is a lower-ranking rule that does not override this.

Yes: under art. 71, comma 13-bis of D.Lgs. 81/2008, the Corpo nazionale dei vigili del fuoco may carry out itself the periodic verifications of comma 11 for Allegato VII equipment it owns or holds on loan, and variable-inclination aerial ladders are listed in Allegato VII.

rows.text: Under Article 52(2) of Regulation (EU) 2023/1230 (REG.md), EC type-examination certificates issued under Article 12 of Directive 2006/42/EC remain valid until they expire.

Regulation (EU) 2023/1230, Article 6(11) provides for delegated acts 'if necessary after the Commission report referred to in Article 53(3)' but states no date by which they must be adopted; Article 47(2) only sets the five-year period of delegation from 19 July 2023.
Article 71, paragraph 14 of Legislative Decree 81/2008 sets no time limit for the decree amending the Annex VII equipment list; the 12-month deadline in paragraph 13 concerns a different decree.
